triage_candidates.statement: NOTHING IN g1 TIES A PAGE'S LOCATION TO ITS CONTENT. Measured, not argued (.agent-work/issue-456/evidence/g1-undesigned-attacks.txt): swapping the CONTENTS of two entity pages, and renaming helper.md to Helper.md while leaving its title alone, each pass all six checks with exit 0. Both produce a map whose module-index links send a reader to the wrong page or to a 404. Every content check in this gate classifies a page by its TITLE, deliberately, so none of them can see it. The natural owner is g4, whose close criteria already require 'a GRAPH WALK that follows links rather than trusting layout' -- that walk should assert both that every link resolves and that the target page's title matches the link text. NOT built here because a link-format assertion is a render-shape assertion and g1 carries none.

'DROP A sorted()' IS NOT UNIFORMLY A DETERMINISM DEFECT, and the g1 determinism check should not be read as if it were. The designed mutation drops sorted() around a SET comprehension in module_index, which is hash-ordered and correctly caught. Dropping the sorted() around the CALLER list is not caught, and that is right:  is a Counter, so list(callers) yields insertion order, which is fixed by the statement order in the store and identical under every hash seed. The rendered caller list simply stops being alphabetical. Consequence for later gates: a determinism check can only see orderings that come from a hash, so g5 (caller split) must not treat a green determinism run as evidence that its ordering is stable or sensible -- ordering-of-presentation belongs to gB.

SUPERSEDES tc2, which lost one word to shell backtick expansion when it was filed -- read this one instead. DROPPING A sorted() IS NOT UNIFORMLY A DETERMINISM DEFECT, and the g1 determinism check must not be read as if it were. The designed mutation drops sorted() around a SET comprehension in module_index; a set is hash-ordered, so it is correctly caught. Dropping the sorted() around the CALLER list is NOT caught, and that is correct: the caller map is a collections.Counter, so iterating it yields insertion order, which is fixed by the statement order in the store and identical under every hash seed. The rendered caller list merely stops being alphabetical. Consequence for later gates: a determinism check can only see orderings that come from a hash, so g5 (the caller split) must not treat a green determinism run as evidence that its ordering is stable or sensible. Ordering-of-presentation is a render shape and belongs to gB.

why_trail.why: Context loaded and ground truth measured before writing anything: a fresh full build of this repo takes 7.5s and reports pages=3648 modules=112 entities=3536 entity_pages=3536, so pages-1-modules=3535 != 3536 -- the handoff's RED invariant reproduces exactly, and map/scripts.run_skill_eval/ holds Verdict.md with no verdict.md beside it. checks.py today prints and returns a literal 0.

checks.py rewritten around a MapUnderCheck that reads the stores and the page tree directly rather than through render.load_stores, plus a CHECKS registry whose run() returns 1 when any check fails. A missing page tree or missing store is now a FAILURE, not a skip -- the vacuous-pass shape test_mutation_floor pins for map_orient. First real check: no-empty-pages (tc26).

Determinism lands as two builds in SEPARATE processes with different hash seeds, compared byte-for-byte; tree_diff names every differing path rather than returning a boolean. The separate-process detail is load-bearing: a string hash seed is fixed for a process's life, so two builds inside one process share it and a hash-ordered listing looks perfectly stable. Nothing in the shipped tree was mutated -- the attack runs against a copied package, which also gives every later check a red proof harness.

The inbound check re-derives every page's caller set from a second, independently-written pass over the raw statement store (checks.StoreScan) and compares it to the RENDERED page text, not to the renderer's own inbound dict -- so a check whose expected value came from the code under test is structurally impossible here. Proven red two ways against a copied package: dropping 'reads' from the inbound predicates (under-reported sites) and attributing an edge to the callee's module instead of the caller's (every cross-module dependency hidden). Both mutations still build and still render plausible numbers; only the second derivation tells them from the truth. Positive control: the unmutated copy passes. Green on the real corpus and on the synthetic cross-module fixture, which is deliberately wide enough (5 sites, 2 modules, one of them the page's own) that a check dropping half the edges would still be caught.

Two page-local checks land. refs-line-self-consistent asserts the arithmetic the rendered line must satisfy at any numbers (no module named twice, never more named than counted, at most ONE counted module unnamed -- the page's own, sites >= modules, zero-and-zero arriving together) and it scans EVERY page in the tree, which is the scope inbound-attribution cannot reach. entity-symbol-join cross-checks the (file,line) join's OUTPUT against a third fact neither AST pass shares -- the entity's own leaf name -- and compares leaves only, so D2's truncated chains do not make it red at g2 for the wrong reason. Both relational; neither pins a count or a rendered shape.

page-accounting ships with TWO arms. COVERAGE (shape-free): every module and every entity the store declares must be the title of some page; it never says where a page lives or what it is called, so no later gate moves it. COUNT: pages == 1 + modules + entities, the identity the render report contradicts, and the one that is red today. Coverage is asserted on its own rather than only reported when the count is off -- attacking my own count arm found the hole: delete one page and add one stray page and the arithmetic balances while an advertised page is gone; there is now a test for exactly that. The named constant TOP_INDEX_PAGES is the single place a later index tier has to update, deliberately rather than silently. Nothing here re-counts the tree to make entity_pages agree (tc24) and nothing renames anything (g2).

Every check in the gate has now been attacked by something its author did not design for it, including the three inherited ones. The pass paid for itself twice: it exposed a hole in my own count arm (delete one page, add one stray page, the books balance) which is now closed by a separate coverage arm with its own test, and it turned two of StoreScan's declared limits from prose into measurements. Four survivors named plainly, two of them real gaps, routed to g4 as tc1 and recorded as tc3 rather than papered over by narrowing any check's claim. Working tree restored: only checks.py and test_code_map.py are modified; every mutation ran against a COPY of the package.
